item.title: Jinan University marks 120th founding anniv.
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
A drone photo taken on Nov. 11, 2026 shows the Tsang Hin-chi Science Hall inside the Shipai campus of Jinan University in Guangzhou, south China's Guangdong Province. Jinan University marks its 120th founding anniversary on Monday. As China's first state-established university for overseas Chinese, it is known as the country's leading institution of higher education for overseas Chinese. The name "Jinan" reflects its mission to reach out to overseas Chinese communities and spread Chinese culture around the world. Founded in Nanjing in 1906, the university now has five campuses across Guangzhou, Shenzhen and Zhuhai in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. It offers programs across 12 broad academic disciplines, including humanities, sciences, engineering and medicine. The university has 17 disciplines ranked among the world's top 0.5 percent in the Essential Science Indicators (ESI) rankings, including six in the top 0.1 percent. Its pharmacology and toxicology discipline ranks among the world's top 0.05 percent. The number of high-level professionals at the university has increased by 92.8 percent over the past five years. Since its founding, the university has educated more than 600,000 students from over 170 countries and regions, including Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan. item.title: Policy synergy supports China's steady growth
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- China's economy maintained overall stability in October, with new growth drivers strengthening and the economic structure improving, as enhanced policy coordination helped underpin solid growth, official data showed on Monday. The National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) said the value-added industrial output of enterprises rose 4.8 percent year on year in October, while the service production index increased 4.6 percent last month. The surveyed urban unemployment rate stood at 5.1 percent, down 0.1 percentage point from September, and the consumer price index rose 0.7 percent year on year. In the January-October period, retail sales of goods and services, a major indicator of the country's consumption strength, expanded 2.5 percent year on year, with service retail sales up 4.9 percent. China's goods imports and exports totaled 44.81 trillion yuan (about 6.67 trillion U.S. dollars), surging by 20 percent. China's fixed-asset investment, meanwhile, dropped 8.1 percent year on year in the first 10 months of 2026. Excluding the property sector, the country's fixed-asset investment decreased by 5.1 percent in the first 10 months of the year. Investment in intellectual property products rose 9.2 percent, pointing to a shift toward innovation-driven growth. The steady momentum came as China strengthened coordination of existing and incremental policies, channeling resources into innovation, industrial upgrading and new quality productive forces. As a result, high-tech manufacturing value-added jumped 17.6 percent in October, and equipment manufacturing value-added grew 10.6 percent. Production of 3D-printing equipment, lithium-ion batteries and industrial robots surged 85.9 percent, 30 percent and 26 percent, respectively, while new energy vehicle output rose 17.1 percent. NBS spokesperson Fu Linghui said the economy maintained overall stability in October and continued the momentum of "new driving forces and improved structure." New growth drivers, represented by high-end and smart manufacturing, contributed more than half of the growth in industrial value-added in the first 10 months of 2026. Foreign trade was a bright spot. China's goods imports and exports in October climbed 31.2 percent year on year to 4.87 trillion yuan, with exports up 28.7 percent and imports increasing by 34.7 percent. In the January-October period, trade with Belt and Road partner countries increased 18.5 percent, trade by private enterprises rose 20.1 percent, and exports of mechanical and electrical products grew by 25.2 percent. Exports of high-tech products and that of the "new three," namely photovoltaic products, lithium-ion batteries and electric vehicles, all soared by more than 50 percent in October, Fu said. "The seamless transition between new and traditional growth drivers is the result of our persistent and steady efforts over many years to promote high-quality development," noted Wang Guanhua, another NBS spokesperson. "It is something we have long anticipated and hoped for, and it will provide stronger support for the economy going forward." However, Fu cautioned that the international environment remains unstable and uncertain, the imbalance between supply and demand at home is still prominent, and some enterprises face operational difficulties. The foundation for steady economic improvement still needs to be consolidated, he explained. "Next, efforts should be made to ensure the effective implementation of policies, further unleash domestic demand potential, optimize supply, deepen reform and opening up, enhance development momentum and vitality, and improve people's livelihoods," Fu added. China's gross domestic product grew 4.6 percent year on year in the first three quarters of 2026, and the October data suggested that this steady performance remained intact despite domestic and external headwinds, according to Wang. Wang said coordinated macro policies will help the economy continue its innovation-driven, high-quality and improved development, providing support and conditions for achieving the full-year growth target. China is targeting economic growth of 4.5 percent to 5 percent in 2026 and will strive for better in practice, this year's government work report noted. ■

item.title: Shenyang Palace Museum in northeast China marks centennial with porcelain donation
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
Tourists visit an exhibition at the Shenyang Palace Museum in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Nov. 16, 2026. The Shenyang Palace Museum celebrated its centennial on Monday, and received a donation of 41 porcelain pieces as a birthday gift. To mark its centennial this year, the museum is hosting multiple exhibitions highlighting its history, including an exhibition of 100 of its most precious items and another featuring photographs from the past century. (Xinhua/Li Gang) SHENYANG, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- The Shenyang Palace Museum in the capital city of northeast China's Liaoning Province celebrated its centennial on Monday, and received a donation of 41 porcelain pieces as a birthday gift. The donated collection, all export porcelain spanning three major categories, fills a blank in the museum's export porcelain holdings and further improves the collection system, said Zhang Guobin, director of the collection department of the museum. These pieces were donated by Zhao Qiang, chairman of the Macau Association for Preservation of Cultural Relics. "These porcelain pieces once crossed mountains and seas to reach the world. Today, they have entered the museum. It is my hope that through research and display, they can tell more stories of the exchange between Chinese culture and the world," he said. Shenyang Palace Museum, where the former imperial complex of three emperors of the Qing Dynasty (1644-1911) was located, was set up in 1926 and opened to the public in 1929. In 2004, it was added to the World Cultural Heritage List. To mark its centennial this year, the museum is hosting multiple exhibitions highlighting its history, including an exhibition of 100 of its most precious items and another featuring photographs from the past century. Over the years, the museum has conducted a series of activities. Through innovative exhibitions and creative cultural products, it has showcased its architectural and cultural relics, as well as the culture behind them. By Nov. 1, Shenyang Palace Museum had received more than 6 million visitors this year, setting a new record high. ■ A tourist visits an exhibition at the Shenyang Palace Museum in Shenyang, northeast China's Liaoning Province, Nov. 16, 2026. item.title: Practical cooperation, digital ties chart China-ASEAN course for shared future
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
MANILA, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- As a landmark outcome of the 49th ASEAN Summit and Related Summits, the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement was signed on Saturday in Manila, aiming to bolster a regional digital economy that is expected to reach 2 trillion U.S. dollars by 2030. Described as "the world's first most comprehensive regional agreement on the digital economy," it marks a major milestone in the 11-member bloc's journey toward an open, secure, interoperable, competitive and inclusive digital economy. Over the past few years, the digital economy, represented by artificial intelligence (AI), cross-border e-commerce and mobile payments, has played an increasingly important role in China-ASEAN economic and trade relations. Experts said the signing of the agreement, along with Monday's announcement of the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol to take effect on Dec. 1, will further strengthen practical cooperation among member states and lay a more solid foundation for shared regional growth. BUILDING A SHARED DIGITAL ECOSYSTEM Based in south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, the RunDo platform run by Runjian Co., Ltd is translating China-ASEAN cooperation in the digital economy into tangible applications. Using drones and AI to oversee the operation of nearly 3,000 solar power sites in Malaysia, with a combined capacity of nearly 300 megawatts, the platform has significantly reduced the need for manual inspections. "The platform has boosted maintenance efficiency by over 30 percent and cut labor costs by more than 20 percent," said Yang Yexi, marketing manager of the company's Guangxi branch. By drawing on computing infrastructure in Nanning, capital of China's Guangxi, ASEAN firms can access models and computing power remotely without building large centers of their own, Yang said, noting that Runjian has already launched more than 80 such computing projects across the region. In infrastructure development, China has established cross-border terrestrial fiber-optic cable networks connecting with Vietnam, Laos, and Myanmar. Chinese companies have also helped advance 5G in Thailand and build data centers in Malaysia, expanding digital access across the region. Mobile payment services are another area of the growing China-ASEAN cooperation. In April, Chinese digital payment platform WeChat Pay announced that users could make payments in countries including Thailand, Malaysia and Singapore by scanning local QR codes. With the signing of the ASEAN Digital Economy Framework Agreement and the inclusion of a dedicated digital economy chapter in the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area 3.0 Upgrade Protocol, regional cooperation in this field is poised to deepen further. The prospects for digital economy cooperation between China and ASEAN are promising, said Lye Liang Fook, associate senior fellow at ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute. He noted that both sides should step up efforts to develop secure digital infrastructure, including 5G networks and undersea cables, supported by reliable supplies of renewable energy. They should also accelerate cross-border digitalization through the use of e-certificates and electronic documents to reduce transaction costs for micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, which account for more than 90 percent of all enterprises in Southeast Asia, Lye said. SOLID FOUNDATION FOR COOPERATION In recent years, many ASEAN countries have ramped up investment and rolled out initiatives to accelerate the development of their digital economies. Indonesia, for instance, has released a white paper outlining its digital economy development plans through 2030, with a focus on expanding digital finance and e-commerce. Thailand, meanwhile, has approved 34 data center and data hosting projects worth a combined 21.34 billion dollars since 2025, as it seeks to position itself as a regional hub for digital infrastructure. Against this backdrop, ASEAN countries are increasingly looking to deepen digital cooperation with China, as they believe bilateral digital cooperation rests on a solid foundation. China and ASEAN have a strong foundation for digital economy cooperation because the two sides complement each other, said Tinn Wong, a research fellow with Malaysia's Center for Advanced Studies and Research. China has a relatively advanced digital economy, while ASEAN, home to around 680 million people, offers a growing consumer market with a young population and rising demand for digital services and infrastructure, he said, adding that these complementary strengths create significant opportunities for cooperation between the two sides. Lucio Pitlo, a member of the board of directors of the Philippine Association for Chinese Studies, noted that China has a well-developed digital commerce sector, robust digital connectivity, and strong capabilities in fintech and logistics. He added that China could also help ASEAN strengthen the security and integrity of online transactions through capacity building in cybersecurity. Similarly, Lye said that ASEAN countries vary in their capacity to tap into opportunities in the digital and green economies. While some urgently need to upgrade their digital infrastructure, others lack the necessary know-how, technical expertise and skilled workforce. "These are areas where China can assist and be of great help," he said. FROM DIGITAL SYNERGY TO SHARED FUTURE Digital economy cooperation can add a new dimension to China-ASEAN relations, Wong said. He noted that beyond trade and investment, it is about forging closer economic ties and ensuring that both sides remain competitive in an increasingly digital global economy. As the China-ASEAN Free Trade Area has progressed from tariff cuts on most goods in Version 1.0 to greater market access to services and investment in Version 2.0, and now to Version 3.0 covering areas such as the digital economy and green development, the digital economy has become an important driver of bilateral economic and trade growth, bringing the two sides closer. Amid a complex and volatile international landscape, China and ASEAN have further consolidated their status as each other's most active investment partners. In 2025, two-way trade exceeded 1 trillion dollars for the first time. China has remained ASEAN's largest trading partner for 17 consecutive years, while ASEAN has been China's largest trading partner for six years in a row. From traditional trade and investment to emerging areas such as the digital economy, green and low-carbon development, and industrial and supply chain cooperation, the map of China-ASEAN collaboration continues to expand. The China-Laos Railway and the Jakarta-Bandung High-Speed Railway are operating smoothly, while Malaysia's East Coast Rail Link is scheduled to begin commercial passenger services in mid-December. These flagship connectivity projects are not only supporting regional development but also helping lay a solid foundation for a closer China-ASEAN community with a shared future. ■

item.title: Riding the wave of innovation: Xi's vision for Asia-Pacific's next chapter
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Self-driving minibuses zooming through city streets, delivery drones buzzing overhead and futuristic skyscrapers dotting the skyline -- Qianhai, a reform and innovation zone in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen, offers a vivid snapshot of China's urban future. Back in December 2012, when Xi Jinping visited Shenzhen on his first domestic inspection tour after being elected general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee, the transformation of the district's barren tidal flats was still underway. In the years that followed, what many called a "special zone within a special zone" has evolved into an innovation hub connecting China with the wider Asia-Pacific, mirroring Shenzhen's own remarkable journey from a small fishing village to a global high-tech metropolis. Later this week, the Chinese president is set to host leaders and representatives from APEC economies in Shenzhen, where they are expected to discuss how the Asia-Pacific can better serve as a driving force for innovation and high-quality development across the region and beyond. SURGING TIDE The APEC meeting is held at a time of challenges and opportunities for the global economy. While the rapid advance of frontier technologies is opening up new horizons, lackluster economic growth and mounting development hurdles continue to weigh on the global economy. Innovation has been a recurring theme in Xi's participation in APEC meetings since his debut at the forum in 2013. In Xi's view, innovation has fueled the economic takeoff of the Asia-Pacific. He has urged APEC economies to make innovation a key driver of growth. Riding the wave of economic globalization in the early 1990s, APEC adopted an innovative organizational model to deepen economic interdependence and explore new avenues for regional cooperation in finance, industry and digital development. Today, the Asia-Pacific remains the world's fastest-growing region and accounts for more than 60 percent of global GDP. Innovation has also been a defining feature of China's own development under Xi's leadership. He has made innovation-powered development a national strategy, stressing that in this new round of global growth, only the reformers and innovators will emerge stronger and win. With a keen eye on breakthroughs in frontier technologies, Xi has made frequent visits to the leading drivers of scientific and technological innovation, including incubators and industrial parks, during inspection tours across China. He tested smart glasses, watched demonstrations of humanoid robots, and experienced newly developed domestic vehicles. Xi has called for the development of new quality productive forces, emphasizing the role of technological innovation in replacing old growth drivers and putting China's development on a more sustainable footing. Today, as the Asia-Pacific needs more than ever to tap new growth potential amid an unfolding technological revolution, Xi has encouraged APEC economies to boldly ride the crest of the innovation wave. "We should fully harness new technologies to empower and propel us forward," he told the APEC meeting in Gyeongju, South Korea, last year. Xi believes that the Asia-Pacific should "remain the locomotive of economic globalization in the future." Facing profound changes in global dynamics, regional economies "cannot afford to be just onlookers." Shenzhen, a showcase of China's innovation-driven development, will provide a fitting backdrop for discussions among APEC members on advancing innovation across the region. China's role as "an important source of investment and technology and a key hub of regional supply chains is increasingly shaping economic opportunities across the Asia-Pacific," said Haiping Zhang, director of the New Zealand APEC Study Center at the University of Auckland. "FERTILE GROUND" In Xi's view, the Asia-Pacific should become "a fertile ground for scientific breakthroughs and a pacesetter for innovation." That requires the region to accelerate the digital, intelligent and green transformation of its economies. Xi has committed to advancing this transformation by deepening cooperation in technology between China and other APEC economies. During his Southeast Asia tour in April 2025, two of the three destinations -- Malaysia and Vietnam -- are APEC economies. Xi reached agreements with both countries to deepen cooperation in frontier areas, including the digital economy and artificial intelligence, and to promote exchanges between research institutions and businesses. In fact, local communities in APEC economies are already benefiting from Chinese technology. In Johor state, Malaysia, farmers can predict the growth of durians with an AI system to improve operational efficiency. With the system jointly developed with Xiamen University Malaysia, an overseas campus of a Chinese university, durians can reach Chinese consumers just 36 hours after harvest. Across the Pacific, the Chancay Port on Peru's coast is serving as a green, smart gateway linking Latin America and Asia not merely through shipping routes, but also by the application of advanced technologies. A project directly promoted by Xi, the port was inaugurated in November 2024 during his visit to the South American country and attendance at that year's APEC gathering. Featuring giant automated gantry cranes, low-carbon autonomous trucks and an ecologically designed shoreline, the megaport has handled more than 3.6 billion U.S. dollars in trade and generated around 476 million dollars in tax revenue as of June this year. Alongside efforts to advance cooperation in practical innovation, Xi has also stressed the importance of fostering an enabling environment that unleashes innovative potential and removes barriers to progress. In July this year, China announced it would establish a center in Qianhai to promote APEC cooperation on cross-border data flows. Xi's advocacy for building an open economic environment in the region is reflected in China's own commitment to further deepening reform and promoting high-standard opening-up. Measures such as shortening the negative list for foreign investment and applying visa-free policies, together with connectivity initiatives, have facilitated the flow of knowledge and technologies between China and the rest of the world. China's efforts to facilitate trade, improve logistics and infrastructure, and foster greater integration of supply and value chains can help developing economies integrate more fully into regional and international trade, said Marcela Vera, an economist at Chile's University of Santiago. "China has placed greater emphasis on linking trade and investment with technology transfer, industrial upgrading and the extension of value chains. If such cooperation deepens further, Pacific Rim economies will be better positioned to increase the added value of their products through technological collaboration and industrialization," she added. SYMPHONY FOR ALL The sweeping new scientific revolution and industrial transformation underway are having a profound impact on modes of production, ways of life and human values. Xi once warned that if not handled properly, the wealth gap between the North and the South could further widen. In his view, the fruits of innovation "should benefit the entire humanity" in a fairer and more inclusive manner. At the handover ceremony of last year's APEC meeting, Xi pledged China's readiness to "bring all parties together to advance the goal of an Asia-Pacific community." His proposal is rooted in his vision of building an Asia-Pacific community with a shared future. Xi first articulated this notion in 2013, calling on APEC members to leverage their own development to drive the development of others and, ultimately, achieve more coordinated growth. Xi's push for the inclusive development of AI serves as a prime example. In Xi's own words, AI development should be "a symphony of international cooperation." APEC economies have recognized the urgency of making AI development more inclusive and strengthening governance. This shared understanding was reflected in the adoption of the APEC AI Initiative at last year's meeting in South Korea. In July, Xi announced the creation of the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organization, a public good for improving global AI governance, at the 2026 World AI Conference and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance. "We must carry out extensive international cooperation and help Global South countries with capacity building to bridge the AI and digital divides, promote sustainable development, and prevent creating new historical injustice in AI," he said. At the conference, Xi also offered 30 countries access to China's MAZU, an AI-powered meteorological warning system, to help narrow gaps in disaster prevention and mitigation capacity. "By enabling more countries to strengthen their capacity for development and more people to lead happier lives, the Asia-Pacific can achieve shared prosperity and offer certainty to the world," said Wirun Phichaiwongphakdee, director of the Thailand-China Research Center of the Belt and Road Initiative. Just as Xi himself has said, "The future of Asia-Pacific belongs to each and every member of this big family." ■

item.title: Shenzhen summit marks first face-to-face meeting among Chinese, Russian, U.S. heads of state in history: spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- The meeting of the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state in south China's Shenzhen will be the first face-to-face meeting in history involving the top leaders of the three countries, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said on Monday. Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Nov. 19, according to the ministry. Mao said the heads of state will have an in-depth exchange of views on maintaining world peace and promoting strategic stability in major country relations, which is of groundbreaking significance. Noting that China, Russia and the United States are all founding members of the UN and permanent members of the UN Security Council, Mao said the three countries have fought together to achieve the victory of the World Anti-Fascist War. Under current circumstances, the three countries shoulder the important responsibility of cooperating to address global challenges and promote world peace and stability, said Mao. Strengthening communication, managing and controlling differences, and stabilizing relations among China, Russia and the United States serve the interests of the three countries, meet the expectations of the international community, and are conducive to stabilizing the world situation and promoting dialogue and cooperation, she said. ■

item.title: Xi congratulates Jinan University on its 120th founding anniversary
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
BEIJING, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday sent a congratulatory letter to Jinan University, celebrating its 120th founding anniversary. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, extended congratulations to the faculty, students and alumni of the university. Xi urged the university to carry forward its patriotic traditions and distinctive educational features, and to foster more young talent among compatriots in Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan and overseas Chinese. He also called on the university to carry forward and promote Chinese culture and advance friendly exchanges between China and the world. The university was asked to improve its education and teaching quality and make new contributions to pooling strength among overseas Chinese and advancing Chinese modernization. Founded in 1906, the university in south China's Guangdong Province has, over the past 120 years, nurtured a wealth of outstanding talent for Hong Kong, Macao and Taiwan, as well as for more than 170 countries. ■

item.title: Xi urges breaking new ground in high-quality development of Greater Bay Area
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-16
ZHONGSHAN, Guangdong, Nov. 16 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping on Monday urged efforts to thoroughly study and implement the guiding principles of the fifth plenary session of the 20th Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, and to strive to break new ground in the high-quality development of the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks during an inspection tour in Zhongshan, south China's Guangdong Province. Stressing fully and faithfully implementing the decisions and arrangements made at the plenary session and leveraging new progress in persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance, Xi urged a better job in advancing integrated development along the Pearl River Estuary. Visiting an artificial island of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, a sea-crossing project connecting the cities of Shenzhen, Zhongshan and Guangzhou, Xi demanded efforts to further enhance the management and operation of this mega transport project to better serve the development of the Greater Bay Area. At an industrial park in Zhongshan, Xi learned about local efforts to absorb industrial transfers, transform and upgrade traditional industries, and develop emerging industries. Building the Greater Bay Area is a major strategic plan made by the CPC Central Committee, Xi said, calling on cities along the Pearl River Estuary including Guangzhou, Shenzhen, Zhuhai, Dongguan and Zhongshan to play a pioneering role. Xi expressed the hope that Zhongshan would seize the opportunities, take reform and innovation as the fundamental driving force, improve regional cooperation mechanisms, foster a sound business environment, and vigorously promote the deep integration of technological innovation and industrial innovation. Speaking to representatives of small and medium-sized enterprises and sci-tech personnel, Xi encouraged them to make greater contributions to the development of Guangdong and the Greater Bay Area and China's greater self-reliance and strength in science and technology. Xi also visited the Museum of Dr. Sun Yat-sen and laid a floral basket before his bronze statue. This year marks the 160th anniversary of Sun's birth. On the new journey, it is necessary to emulate, inherit and promote his invaluable spirit, and inspire all Chinese people at home and abroad to unite and strive to build a great country and advance national rejuvenation through Chinese modernization, Xi said. During the inspection tour, Xi also stressed the need to continuously steer the economy toward innovation-driven and high-quality development, ensure that major targets and tasks for the year are fulfilled, and get the 15th Five-Year Plan (2026-2030) off to a good start. ■
